physicalNotes: Radius 0.824 Jupiter radii from Psaridi et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..39P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A..39P/abstract): 58,909.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.303 Jupiter masses (Psaridi et al. 2023, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2023A&A...675A..39P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A..39P/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 6.40252947289 d
sources.shape: Psaridi et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..39P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PSARIDI_ET_AL__2023): a/R* 10.637; Psaridi et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..39P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PSARIDI_ET_AL__2023): inclination 86.62 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460006.078147 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
